title: Oncall handshake procedures and automated status flows
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the "handshake" and continuity procedures for on-call rotations and a companion set of deterministic automated status flows that reduce human overhead during incident startup. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, customer success, and anyone who will author or consume engineer-to-customer communications during outages.

Goals

- Ensure reliable, brief, repeatable handoffs between on-call shifts and between teams.
- Minimize time-to-first-public-communication by automating status page updates and internal paging where safe.
- Provide templated, role-specific communications for initial, cadence, and resolution updates.
- Capture ownership and escalation rules so incidents progress without decision paralysis.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood public-facing production services and model inference endpoints in hosted and Dedicated deployments. Excludes purely internal tooling flagged non-customer-impacting by the service owner.

Definitions

- Handshake: the short, written + verbal exchange that confirms ownership and context between outgoing and incoming on-call engineers.
- Incident Automation Flow: a set of automated steps (alerts -> runbook -> status update) that run with minimal human intervention until escalation thresholds are reached.
- Incident ID: standardized identifier: RWI-{YYYYMMDD}-{SEQ} (generated by incident manager).

Roles & Responsibilities

- Primary On‑Call (POC): first responder; responsible for initial triage and containment.
- Incident Commander (IC): takes ownership if incident escalates beyond containment (typically after 20 minutes or at SLO breach risk).
- Incident Communicator (IComm): owns public status updates and customer comms; liaises with Customer Success for major-impact incidents.
- SRE Lead / Pager Duty Escalation: coordinates multi-team mobilization and postmortem assignment.
- Outgoing On‑Call: completes handshake checklist and documents outstanding work.

Handoff (Handshake) Checklist — mandatory before leaving shift

1. Open the incident management page for any active incidents and confirm ownership. If no incident, perform a shift transfer note.
2. Provide a 5–10 minute verbal summary to incoming on-call with these items: active incidents, key mitigation state, recent alerts suppressed, and any scheduled tasks that may affect availability.
3. Post a written handoff into the team channel using the template below. Include: timestamp, active incidents (IDs), mitigation actions performed, outstanding actions, and CI/CD or infra changes in last 24 hours.
4. Confirm monitoring alarms and alert forwarding are functioning: check latest PagerDuty/Alertmanager health check, and validate status webhook delivery.
5. If any incident is active and not yet assigned an IC, ensure the IC field is set. If no IC yet, agree on escalation trigger (time or threshold).

Handoff template (team channel)

- Shift: <incoming_name> from <HH:MM> UTC
- Outgoing: <name> at <HH:MM> UTC
- Active incidents: RWI-20260210-03 (investigating)
- Summary: brief one-paragraph status
- Actions performed: list
- Outstanding: list
- Alerts muted: list
- Notes: runbook pointers, on-call runbook path, links

Automated Status Flows (design & examples)

We use deterministic automation to ensure rapid public-facing communication and to reduce the cognitive load on first responders. Automation is gated by safety checks: it will not publish customer-impact statements without two independent signals (alert + metric breach) unless an IC authorizes. Flows are implemented as idempotent steps in our incident manager.

Flow states (canonical):

1. detected -> 2. triaged -> 3. investigating -> 4. mitigated -> 5. resolved -> 6. postmortem

Trigger examples and automated actions:

- detected: alert from Alertmanager (error rate > 5% or latency p95 > 3s for 5m)
  - action: create incident ID and page POC, attach initial event snapshot to incident. No public message yet.

- triaged: POC confirms customer impact (metric + user-visible errors)
  - action: if metric breach confirmed, post internal 'investigating' draft and notify IComm; if both conditions true, automation will create a status-page draft and push to 'pending' state.

- investigating: IC or POC marks incident as investigating or automation auto-promotes after N minutes with confirmed impact.
  - action: publish status page 'Investigating' with template A (see below). Start 15-minute cadence timer.

- mitigated: measurable improvement (error rate halved or latency back to within SLO for 10m)
  - action: update status to 'Identified' or 'Monitoring' depending on confidence, change cadence to 30 minutes and include mitigation notes.

- resolved: SLOs restored for 30 minutes and root cause identified or a patch deployed
  - action: publish 'Resolved' notice and schedule postmortem assignment.

Automation safety gates (must pass all to auto-publish):

- two independent signals: alert + metric breach OR alert + customer complaint URL
- no unreviewed deploys in last 15 minutes for the implicated service (checks CI metadata)
- no active PII/secure-data breach tags detected by the incident classifier

Status page templates

Use the following templates verbatim; IComm may add customer-specific detail but must not alter the severity tag without IC approval. Replace placeholders in double braces.

Template A — Initial public notice (Investigating)

Title: {SERVICE} — Investigating degraded performance ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Next update: ~15 minutes
Notes: We are aware of increased error rates affecting {REGION or ROUTE}. Engineers are investigating and we will post updates here.

Template B — Identified / Mitigated

Title: {SERVICE} — Mitigation in progress ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Identified / Under monitoring
Impact: A subset of requests to {ENDPOINT} were affected; mitigation deployed to {REGION}.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Notes: Traffic has been rerouted and error rate has decreased. We are monitoring and expect to provide an update in 30 minutes.

Template C — Resolved

Title: {SERVICE} — Resolved ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
Status: Resolved
Impact: Customer-facing impact has been resolved.
Time: {{UTC_TIMESTAMP}}
Notes: Root cause: brief summary. Remediation: what was changed. Postmortem: link (pending).

Customer-facing email/SMS/CS template (short)

Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {SERVICE} degraded (update)\n
Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

We are aware of degraded performance impacting {SERVICE}. Our engineering team is investigating and we will follow up with another update in ~15 minutes. For updates see: {STATUS_PAGE_LINK} or reply to this message.

— Redwood Inference Support

Customer-facing enterprise template (for large customers; longer form)

Subject: Enterprise notice — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} affecting {SERVICE}

Hi {{CS_LEAD_NAME}} and team,

Summary: brief one-line summary of impact.
Current state: Investigating / Identified / Resolved
Timeline: key timestamps (detection, triage start, mitigation start)
Mitigations in place: list
Action requested: e.g., please confirm whether you’re seeing errors and share logs if relevant.
Contacts: IComm name and on-call primary contact.

SLO and escalation thresholds (examples)

- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 300ms (global)
- Error SLO: failed requests < 0.5%
- Automated publish threshold: error rate > 5% for 5m OR p95 latency > 3s for 5m.
- IC escalation: 20 minutes after triaged state OR when SLO breach risk > 2x baseline.

On-call rotation best practices (practical rules)

- Shift length: standard 8 hours weekday, 12 hours weekend (follow people-ops policy for overtime).
- Pair handoffs for the first week of new hires: outgoing must shadow the incoming for >= 1 hour.
- Limit concurrent maintenance tasks during shift transitions: no risky deploys within 30 minutes of handoff.
- Rotation ownership: each service must have a documented owner and backup (name + PD escalation in the runbook).

Game day curriculum (90-minute template)

1. 0–10m: Setup and roles assigned (IC, IComm, SRE Lead).
2. 10–25m: Inject simulated detection (synthetic traffic causing error spike).
3. 25–45m: Validate automation: ensure detection -> incident created -> status draft created.
4. 45–70m: Force escalation by simulating SLO breach; practice customer comms and cross-team coordination.
5. 70–90m: Post-exercise review and actions: assign 3 concrete fixes and owners.

Postmortem and follow-up process

- Postmortem owner: SRE Lead must assign within 48 hours.
- Draft deadline: 7 business days.
- Required sections: summary, timeline, impact (customer-visible), root cause analysis (5 whys or equivalent), mitigations (short-term), systemic recommendations, and action owners with due dates.
- Severity mapping required for executive summaries: Sev-1 (major outage impacting >25% of customers or >1 region for >30 mins), Sev-2 (partial degradation), Sev-3 (minor).

Runbook maintenance and retirement

- Every runbook must have a "last validated" timestamp and a tester name. Runbooks older than 12 months require revalidation before they can be used as automation targets.
- Runbook retirement process: add "deprecated" tag, schedule an owner to migrate callers, and archive old playbooks with cross-links.

Metrics we capture on every incident

- Time to acknowledge (goal < 2 minutes)
- Time to first public communication (goal < 15 minutes when automation gates satisfied)
- Time to mitigation (goal depends on service tier, e.g., < 60 minutes for core inference)
- Mean time to restore (MTTR)
- Postmortem action completion rate (target 95% on-time)

Appendix: automation snippets and examples

Example: create an incident in our incident manager (pseudo-curl)

```
curl -X POST "https://inc-man.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service":"inference-api","title":"Investigating increased error rate","detected_at":"2026-02-12T14:03:00Z","metrics":{"error_rate":0.072}}'
```

Example: update status page draft (idempotent)

```
curl -X PATCH "https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/drafts/{{DRAFT_ID}}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status":"investigating","body":"...templated body..."}'
```

Example: incident handoff message (Slack formatting)

```
/incident-handshake \nshift_incoming: @alice \nshift_outgoing: @priya \nactive_incidents: RWI-20260212-01 (investigating) \nnotes: failover applied to cluster-3, next check in 15m
```
